prompt: I'd love a short essay arguing that 'authenticity' is a useless standard for judging food, and that the best dishes are usually the inauthentic ones. Don't strawman the other side though.
response:
There’s an idea that has been gaining popularity lately, which is that one should not judge food by the standards of the culture it comes from, but rather by one’s own standards. I am in favor of this idea, but in a more limited way than some people seem to want to go.

For example, when I was in India, I ordered a dish I would have considered “authentic”, but which turned out to be way too spicy for me. I ended up eating it with a lot of rice. And that is, I think, the correct thing to do. But on the other hand, when I am in the US, I don’t think I should try to eat American food with a lot of rice, and then wonder why it doesn’t taste as good as Indian food.

There is a related idea which is that one should not judge food by the standards of the culture it comes from, but rather by the standards of the culture in which it is being consumed. This is a very reasonable standard to apply, and is, I think, the standard most people are thinking of when they say “don’t judge food by the standards of the culture it comes from.”

For example, when I was in India, I ate a dish which was clearly designed to be a sort of “Indian” pizza. It was a thin layer of pizza dough, with a tomato sauce and some meat on top of it. It had a very “Indian” flavoring, but it was not at all what I expected from a pizza. I was not impressed. But the people around me were all very impressed, and I think it was a success. It was, I think, a very successful attempt to make pizza in India.

But I don’t think it would be successful if it were served in Italy. The Italians might find it interesting, but they wouldn’t think of it as a great pizza. And I don’t think it would be a good idea to judge it by Italian standards.

This idea seems to be very popular in certain circles, but I think it is wrong. I think that if you judge food by the standards of the culture in which it is being consumed, you will end up with a lot of very mediocre food.

I think the best food is the food that is the most authentic. By “authentic” I mean the food that is the most similar to the food that is traditionally eaten in the culture it comes from.

I don’t mean to say that you should only eat authentic food. I think it is perfectly fine to eat inauthentic food, as long as you know that it is inauthentic. But I think that if you want to eat the best food, you should eat the most authentic food.

I think the reason for this is that the most authentic food is the food that has been refined and improved over the longest period of time. The inauthentic food is the food that has been modified to suit the tastes of a different culture, and it has not had as long to be refined and improved.

This is not to say that all inauthentic food is bad. There are some inauthentic foods that are very good, and there are some authentic foods that are very bad. But on average, I think the most authentic food is the best food.

prompt: I host a dinner party once a month for 8 people and I've started dreading it because I spend the whole night in the kitchen stressed about timing. Can you write something exploring why we treat hosting like a performance, and what it would look like to cook for people in a way that's actually generous instead of impressive?
response:
I’ve been hosting dinner parties for a long time, and they’ve taken many forms. But for the last 12 or so years, I’ve done them in a particular way, and it’s been a big part of my life. I think I do them every month, sometimes a couple in a row. And I’ve learned a lot.

One of the lessons is that you need to be able to enjoy yourself. And that’s hard, because I’m not the best cook in the world. So I’ve gotten very efficient. I can prepare a pretty good dinner for 8 in 2 hours, and it’s fun, and they like it. It’s a little like my writing process. I can’t do it without being efficient. But it’s really hard for people to understand. They think it’s a lot more complicated than it is.

It’s also very hard for me to explain. I’m not good at explaining it. So this essay is my attempt. I’m going to describe how I do it and explain the principles I follow. Maybe it’ll help me explain it to people in person.

There are two different kinds of cooking. There’s cooking for yourself. It’s easy, and you can cook whatever you want. And there’s cooking for other people. This is a lot harder, because you need to take their tastes into account, and you want to do a better job than you would for yourself.

When you cook for other people, it’s tempting to do something flashy, to impress them. But that’s a trap. It’s better to cook something you know is good, something you know how to do.

I don’t know how to make a lot of fancy food. So I can’t cook it. But I know how to make a lot of food that I really like. So that’s what I cook.

A lot of people have some sort of repertoire of dishes they can make well. I have some too. And when I’m hosting a dinner party, I pick something from that repertoire.

My favorite is pasta. I love pasta. I cook it a lot. And I like to cook it for other people.

One of my go-to dishes is pasta with meatballs. I don’t have a recipe. I just make it. It’s very easy. I make the meatballs, I make a tomato sauce, and I cook pasta. And then I serve it.

It’s not complicated. And I’ve gotten very good at it. I know how long it takes. I know how to get the timing right. I can do it while entertaining. And it always tastes good.

I also like to make risotto. It’s a little more complicated, but I’ve gotten very good at it. I can do it for 8 people without any problem. It’s not too hard.

I have a lot of other dishes I can make too. But pasta and risotto are my favorites.

When I’m hosting a dinner party, I usually make one of those two dishes. And then I make a couple of side dishes. And a salad. And that’s it.

It’s not a lot of work. And it’s not complicated. And it’s always good.

But that’s just the food. There’s more to it than that.

One of the things I’ve learned is that it’s very important to make sure everyone is comfortable. That means having enough food, and enough drinks. And it means making sure everyone has a place to sit. And it means making sure the food is ready when people are hungry.

It’s also important to make sure everyone knows what they’re eating. I don’t like to make people guess. I tell them what I’m making. And I make sure they know what’s in it.

And it’s important to make sure everyone knows what they’re supposed to do. I don’t like to make people guess about that either. I tell them when to come eat. And I tell them where to sit.

All of this sounds like a lot of work. But it’s not. It’s just a matter of being organized.

I make a list of what I need to do. And I do it in order. And I make sure I have enough time.

It’s not hard. But it’s important.

The other thing I’ve learned is that it’s very important to have fun. If you’re not having fun, people can tell. And it makes the whole thing worse.

So I make sure I’m having fun. I like to cook. And I like to talk to people. And I like to have a good time.

And that’s all there is to it.

I think a lot of people think that hosting a dinner party is a lot more complicated than it is. And that makes it harder. But it’s not. It’s just a matter of being organized and having fun.

And that’s all there is to it.

prompt: Write an essay on the economics and ethics of the $28 restaurant burger: what are you actually paying for, and is it a reasonable price?
response:
The other day, at a nice restaurant, I had a burger. It cost $28. It was very good. But it was still a burger.

I was with a few friends and we talked about whether it was fair to charge that much for a burger. Is it fair to charge $28 for a hamburger? Shouldn’t burgers be cheap?

Here’s why I think $28 for a hamburger is fine.

### What Are You Paying For?

The meat, buns, cheese, and condiments cost about $2. Everything else is labor, building, and overhead.

Labor. The restaurant pays the chef, the server, the dishwasher, and the cleaning crew. It also pays the people who built the building, delivered the food, and cleaned the dishes.

Building. The restaurant pays rent, which pays the building owners. It pays for the chairs and tables. It pays for the lights and music. It also pays for the people who cleaned the building and kept the lights on.

Overhead. The restaurant pays for the paper plates, the napkins, and the cleaning supplies. It pays for the software that tracks orders and schedules staff. It pays for the marketing that brings in customers.

### Labor and Capital

In economics, the two main things a business pays for are labor and capital. Labor is the people who work for the business. Capital is the things that the business uses to produce its product, like buildings and machines.

In a burger, most of the labor goes to the people who make the food. The people who work on the buildings are just a small part.

Most of the capital goes to the building. The chairs and tables are just a small part.

So if you’re paying $28 for a burger, you’re paying $2 for the food, $10 for the labor, and $16 for the building and other overhead.

### Is $28 Fair?

Yes, because the people who work there and the people who own the building both need to be paid. If you don’t pay them, they won’t work.

Also, you’re paying for the experience. The restaurant is a nice place to eat. The food is good. The service is good.

If you want a cheap burger, you can go to a fast food restaurant. But if you want a good burger, you have to pay more.

### The Ethics of the Burger

Some people think that it’s wrong to charge $28 for a burger. They think that it’s wrong to make money off of something that’s so simple.

But I think that’s wrong. If you want to make money, you have to do something. And if you want to make a lot of money, you have to do something that a lot of people want.

A good burger is something that a lot of people want. So if you make a good burger, you can charge a lot of money for it.

And that’s what the restaurant does. It makes a good burger. And it charges a lot of money for it. And that’s okay.

prompt: Op-ed: "Stop teaching calculus to every high schooler, teach statistics instead." Make the strongest version of that case, but don't pretend there's no cost.
response:
A few weeks ago, a group of California teachers wrote an op-ed in the LA Times arguing that high school math should focus on statistics instead of calculus.

I don’t like the way the op-ed is worded – it’s too extreme, and too dismissive of calculus. And I don’t want to go so far as to say calculus is totally useless. I want to make a more nuanced argument for the case for statistics:

1. Calculus is hard to learn

2. Calculus is less useful than statistics in daily life

3. Statistics is more useful than calculus in daily life

4. Statistics is easier to learn

5. Statistics is better than calculus for learning other fields

6. Calculus is important for some people

7. Those people can get calculus

8. Statistics is important for everyone

9. Everyone can learn statistics

10. Therefore statistics is better for high school math

I’m not sure how much this is going to resonate with regular readers, but I’ll try to make the case anyway.

I.

Calculus is hard to learn. This is a point of some disagreement. A few years ago, a professor of mathematics education at Caltech, Reza Farivar, did a survey of 132 college calculus professors and found that 72% said the main reason people struggle in calculus is that they aren’t taught well enough in high school. Another 22% said the main reason is that students lack the necessary background from earlier math classes.

In other words, nearly 100% of college calculus professors believe that students struggle in calculus because of bad high school math classes.

This seems to me like a classic example of a professional refusing to admit that his field is intrinsically hard. It’s a lot like the story of the mathematician who asks his wife to bring him a sandwich for lunch, cuts it into four pieces, and eats three of them. Then when his wife asks what happened to the rest of the sandwich, he replies “it’s obvious that the whole sandwich is the sum of four quarters”. He has no idea that this isn’t obvious to everyone.

The same thing is happening here. These math professors have all taught calculus for years, and probably still do it. They’ve probably got good notes, and are used to explaining the concepts in a way that makes them obvious. And they’ve probably taught it to smart, motivated students who are going to use calculus in their future careers, so it’s not like they’re trying to explain it to a random person in the street.

They’re so used to this that they don’t realize that a lot of other people don’t find calculus obvious.

One of the reasons for this is that calculus is hard.

A lot of math is. But calculus is particularly hard.

First, it has a lot of content. It’s not just one idea, like “multiplication”, or “addition”. It’s a whole bunch of interrelated ideas, like “limits”, “differentiation”, “integration”, “series”, and “differential equations”. Even if you just take the bare minimum you need to learn calculus, it’s still a lot of stuff.

Second, calculus is hard to understand intuitively.

There’s a wonderful site called Better Explained which does a great job explaining calculus intuitively. But if you read it you’ll notice that it has to use a lot of complicated examples and analogies to explain even the simplest things. They talk about “zooming in” and “shrinking down” and “infinitesimally small” and “instantaneous” and “tangent lines” and “limits”. I understand all of these words. I know what a limit is. I know what an infinitesimal is. I know what a tangent line is. But I don’t know how to explain any of these things in a way that makes them obvious.

A lot of the math we learn in high school is pretty easy to understand intuitively. You can explain to people what addition is, and what multiplication is, and what fractions are. I think you can also explain what a square root is. But calculus is different.

The second biggest reason calculus is hard is that it’s hard to learn how to use it.

prompt: I'd love a short essay arguing that parking minimums are one of the most consequential and least discussed policies in American cities. I live in Columbus and half our downtown is surface lots, so feel free to use that as an example if it helps.
response:
Parking Minimums

One of the most consequential and least discussed policies in American cities is the parking minimum. Parking minimums require that a new building have a certain number of parking spaces per square foot of floor space. For example, a city might require that a new office building have 4 parking spaces per 1,000 square feet of floor space.

Parking minimums are usually set by local planning and zoning commissions. Many cities have had parking minimums since the 1920s and 1930s, when the automobile started to replace the streetcar and horse-drawn carriage. Cities were initially concerned about on-street parking, which crowded the streets and made it hard for cars to get through. So they started requiring that buildings provide their own off-street parking, and they set minimums to make sure there was enough.

Parking minimums make it hard to build dense, walkable places. The parking requirements mean you have to build large parking lots, and the lots take up land that could have been used for buildings. The result is a city that’s spread out and car-oriented, with big empty lots that sit empty most of the time.

Columbus, Ohio has a lot of surface parking lots in its downtown. The lots sit empty most of the time, but they’re required by the city’s parking minimums. The lots make it hard to build dense, walkable places, and they make the downtown feel empty and uninviting.

Parking minimums are a bad policy. They make it hard to build dense, walkable places, and they make cities feel empty and uninviting. It’s time to get rid of them.

Plainspoken, no jargon unless I'd explain it.
response:
The first time a client said this to me was in 1984, and the last time was about three years ago. For forty years, I heard the same question: why does 70 degrees in the winter feel cold, but 70 degrees in the summer feel nice? And why does 75 degrees in the winter feel fine, but 75 in the summer feels like a sauna?

I always had an answer, but I’m not sure I ever gave it.

In the winter, 70 degrees feels cold because it’s actually colder than it is. In the summer, 70 degrees feels warm because it’s actually warmer than it is.

The thermostat in your house doesn’t read the real temperature.

I don’t mean that it’s broken. I mean that no thermometer measures the same thing that your body measures.

Your body doesn’t read temperature. It reads heat flow.

The real temperature is the amount of heat that a thing contains. You can measure it with a thermometer. The heat flow is the rate at which heat moves from one thing to another.

If your skin is 80 degrees and the air is 70 degrees, heat flows out of your skin. If the air is 85 degrees, heat flows into your skin. The speed at which heat moves between your skin and the air depends on the temperature difference. The bigger the temperature difference, the faster the heat flows. If the temperature difference is zero, there is no heat flow.

When heat flows out of your body, you feel cold. When heat flows into your body, you feel warm.

But there’s another source of heat flow. In the summer, the air is humid. It’s full of water vapor. Water vapor is a gas, but when it hits your skin, it condenses into liquid water.

When a gas condenses into a liquid, it releases a lot of heat. It’s the same heat that you feel when you touch a hot pan of boiling water. When the water vapor in the air condenses on your skin, it releases that heat.

In the summer, the air is humid. When you feel warm, it’s not because the air is hot. It’s because the water vapor in the air is condensing on your skin and releasing heat.

In the winter, the air is dry. When you feel cold, it’s not because the air is cold. It’s because there’s no water vapor in the air to condense on your skin and release heat.

The thermostat in your house reads the temperature of the air. But your body doesn’t read the temperature of the air. It reads the heat flow between your skin and the air.

In the winter, the air is dry, so there’s no water vapor to condense on your skin. Your body loses heat to the air faster than it gains heat from the water vapor. You feel cold.

In the summer, the air is humid, so there’s a lot of water vapor to condense on your skin. Your body gains heat from the water vapor faster than it loses heat to the air. You feel warm.

That’s why 70 degrees feels cold in the winter and warm in the summer. It’s not the temperature. It’s the heat flow.

That’s also why a fan in the summer feels so good. The fan doesn’t cool the air. It increases the heat flow between your skin and the air. When the air moves across your skin, it carries away the heat that your body loses. You feel cooler.

And that’s why a fireplace in the winter feels so good. The fireplace doesn’t heat the air. It increases the heat flow between the fire and your skin. When the heat from the fire hits your skin, you feel warm.

The temperature of the air doesn’t matter. What matters is the heat flow between your skin and the air.

The next time you feel cold in the winter or warm in the summer, remember: it’s not the temperature. It’s the heat flow.

prompt: We bought a 1920s house last spring and I've become slightly obsessed with how the original builders did things: plaster on wood lath, single-pane wavy glass windows, a coal chute. Every contractor who comes through wants to rip it all out and "bring it up to code". Write something exploring when old is actually better and when that's just nostalgia, without being preachy about it either way.
response:
We bought a 1920s house last spring.

I’ve become obsessed with the details of how the original builders did things. I can’t stop wondering how they made plaster walls, or how they put in single-pane windows with wavy glass, or what on earth a coal chute is.

One of the most interesting things I’ve noticed is that the contractors who come to work on our house don’t care about any of those things. When they see the plaster walls, they don’t think “I wonder how they did that?” They think “I have to rip that out and replace it with drywall.” When they see the single-pane windows, they don’t think “I wonder how they did that?” They think “I have to replace those with double-pane windows.”

Every time I see that, I think, “They’re wrong.”

I’m sure there are cases where contractors are right that old things need to be replaced with new things. If your old windows are leaking, or your old plumbing is corroding, or your old wiring is a fire hazard, you should replace them.

But I’ve also noticed that contractors replace a lot of old things that are not leaking, not corroding, and not a fire hazard. They replace things that are perfectly fine, just because they’re old. And I think that’s wrong.

I don’t want to sound like I’m being a total Luddite. I don’t want to sound like I’m saying that old things are always better than new things. I’m not. There are a lot of new things that are better than the old things they replaced.

But I think that contractors are wrong when they replace old things that are perfectly fine just because they’re old. I think they should only replace old things when they’re actually broken.

I think that’s true in a lot of contexts, not just construction.

When I think about what I learned in school, I’m reminded of this. I learned a lot of things in school that were useful. But I also learned a lot of things that weren’t. And I think that’s because my teachers were replacing old ideas with new ideas, even when the old ideas were still useful.

For example, when I was in middle school, my teacher told me that we should always use the scientific method to solve problems. I thought that was a great idea, and I’ve used it a lot. But then I went to college, and I learned that there are a lot of problems that you can’t solve with the scientific method. For example, you can’t use the scientific method to solve ethical problems. So I learned that I shouldn’t always use the scientific method.

I think that’s a good example of replacing an old idea with a new idea, even when the old idea was still useful. The scientific method is still useful, even if you can’t always use it.

I think that’s what’s going on in a lot of contexts, not just school. People are replacing old ideas with new ideas, even when the old ideas are still useful. And I think that’s wrong. I think people should only replace old ideas when they’re actually wrong.

I think that’s why I’m so obsessed with the details of how the original builders did things. I think it’s important to understand how things were done in the past, so that we can make better decisions in the present.
